title: Resistor Colour Code Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav opens an old radio and finds tiny beads with coloured stripes and not a single number. The stripes are the label. In this animated lesson we learn the resistor colour code from the ground up: ten colours for the ten digits (B B ROY of Great Britain had a Very Good Wife), gold and silver as multipliers and tolerance, and the four band rule: two digits, a multiplier that counts the zeros, and a tolerance band.

On a live breadboard we decode yellow-violet-red-gold (4.7 kΩ ± 5%), connect it to a 9 V battery and watch the current, then swap in brown-black-orange (10 kΩ) and see the oscilloscope step down. We show what ± 5% really means as a tolerance window, read a five band precision resistor, derive P = VI = I²R = V²/R for the power rating and work out the safe current through a 1 kΩ, ¼ W resistor. Then the exam trap (the third band is a multiplier, not a digit), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 26 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).

In this video:

0:30 The colour code and the mnemonic

2:44 Five band resistors
3:02 Power rating: P = I²R = V²/R
3:35 Worked example: safe current
4:04 Exam trap: the third band
4:23 Where it is asked
